topic: Unlocking Planar Graphs: Euler's Characteristic and Duality

sections.title: Prerequisite: Defining the Planar Graph
lecture_lines: Planar graphs have no crossing edges.
Faces include the infinite outer region.
A house graph has five vertices.
It has six edges, two faces.
animations: Display graph G with nodes and edges. Color: #FFFFFF. [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/house.svg]
Highlight vertices. V becomes V = n. Color: #FF0000.
Highlight edges. E becomes E = m. Color: #00FF00.

sections.title: The Master Equation: Euler's Characteristic
lecture_lines: Euler's formula: V minus E plus F equals 2.
It holds for any connected planar graph.
Look at this simple triangle example.
Three vertices, three edges, two faces.
Three minus three plus two equals two.
animations: Display Euler's formula: V - E + F = 2. Color: #FFFFFF. Include asset [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/triangle.svg].
Highlight V term in formula. Color: #FF0000.
Highlight E term in formula. Color: #00FF00.
Highlight F term in formula. Color: #0000FF.

sections.title: Concept of Duality
lecture_lines: Place a vertex in each face.
Connect dual vertices sharing an edge.
animations: Show dual graph G* nodes at face centers. Color: #FFFF00.
Show edges connecting G* nodes. Color: #00FFFF.

sections.title: Interplay of Duality and Euler
lecture_lines: Dual vertices map to original faces.
Edges remain the same in number.
Faces become vertices in the dual.
animations: Overlay dual graph G* on graph G [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/graph.svg]. Color: #FFFFFF.
Match V* = F and F* = V. Color: #FFFF00.
